plan.summary: Faz 1 Permission System: plan_definitions DB table with 3-tier seed (baslangic/profesyonel/kurumsal), TenantPlanCache with 5min TTL and fail-open strategy, FeatureGuardMiddleware with path-prefix feature checking, 3 new error codes (INV-AUTH-005/006/007), registered in 8 microservices. DB migration renames plan_tier values from English to Turkish.
plan.q_intent: Backend API permission enforcement — tenant plan tier determines which service endpoints are accessible. Closes the security gap where frontend-only feature hiding was the sole enforcement.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: plan_definitions table created with 3 tiers and correct feature matrices
FeatureGuardMiddleware blocks requests when feature not in plan (403 + INV-AUTH-005)
SuperAdmin (TenantId=0) and service calls bypass feature guard
Fail-open: DB unavailable does not block requests
Full solution build PASS with 0 errors

files_changed.change: New: DB-backed plan cache with 5min TTL, fail-open, stale cache fallback
New: Path-prefix feature guard middleware + UseFeatureGuard extension
New: plan_tier rename + plan_definitions table + seed
New: Standalone DDL reference for plan_definitions
Comment update: plan_tier default + features_json description

try_catch_locations: TenantPlanCache.GetAsync — catch(Exception) returns stale cache or null
user_facing_errors: INV-AUTH-005: 403 with Turkish message 'Bu özellik mevcut planınızda bulunmuyor'
error_handling.silent_failure_explanation: All catch blocks log via SystemWarn before returning fallback values. Fail-open design is intentional — feature guard should not be a hard dependency on DB availability.

aha_moments.user_pain: Feature enforcement as single point of failure
aha_moments.aha_moment: DB down doesn't mean all feature-gated endpoints stop working

aha_moments.user_pain: Frontend-only feature enforcement bypassed by API calls
aha_moments.aha_moment: Backend now returns 403 regardless of how the API is called

aha_moments.user_pain: DB query per request for plan data
aha_moments.aha_moment: First request loads from DB, subsequent requests hit in-memory cache

aha_moments.suggestion: Turkish user message with feature name
aha_moments.aha_moment: User knows exactly which feature they're missing

aha_moments.user_pain: Hard to debug why a tenant can't access a feature
aha_moments.suggestion: SystemWarn log with tenant ID, feature name, plan tier, path
aha_moments.aha_moment: Support can grep logs for INV-AUTH-005 to see exactly what was blocked

verification_questions.question: Does the FeatureGuardMiddleware correctly bypass for SuperAdmin (TenantId == 0) and service calls (IsServiceCall)?
When features_json is NULL in tenant_registry, does TenantPlanCache correctly fall back to plan_definitions tier defaults?
If the plan_definitions table does not have a matching tier_name for a tenant's plan_tier, what happens? (LEFT JOIN returns NULL)
Are there any paths that should be guarded but are not, or paths that are guarded but should not be? (e.g., /api/v1/webhook/ in Automation)
